description: Turning Wolfram Language computations into deployed web assets: interactive forms, callable web APIs, cloud objects, embeddable code, scheduled tasks and permission control.

tools.name: FormFunction
tools.description: Creates a web form whose fields are typed with interpreters and whose submission runs a Wolfram Language function on the parsed values. Deploying it produces a live form page. Use it to expose a computation to non-programmers.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Rules from field name to an Interpreter type or a full field specification.

parameters.name: AppearanceRules
parameters.description: Title, description, submit label and other presentation settings.

tools.example:
ff = FormFunction[{"city" -> "City", "days" -> Restricted["Integer", {1, 14}]},
  DateListPlot[WeatherData[#city, "Temperature",
    {DatePlus[Today, -#days], Today, "Day"}]] &, "PNG"];
CloudDeploy[ff, Permissions -> "Public"]
tools.notes: FormPage is the variant that re-displays the form alongside the result after each submission.

tools.name: FormPage
tools.description: Creates a form page that keeps the form visible after submission and shows the result beneath it. It is better suited to exploratory tools than FormFunction, which returns only the result. Field specifications and options are otherwise the same.

tools.name: FormObject
tools.description: Represents a form specification in detail, with control over field types, defaults, labels, hints and validation. It is used inside FormFunction and FormPage when simple field rules are not expressive enough. Use it to build polished forms.

tools.name: APIFunction
tools.description: Defines a web API whose parameters are typed with interpreters and whose body is a Wolfram Language function. Deployed with CloudDeploy it becomes a URL callable from any language. Use it to publish computations as services.
tools.notes: Call the deployed URL with query parameters, for example ?x=2&n=10; URLExecute can call it back from Wolfram code.

tools.name: CloudDeploy
tools.description: Deploys an expression, form, API or notebook to the Wolfram Cloud and returns a CloudObject with a URL. Permissions control who can access it. It is the main publication step for web-facing content.
tools.notes: Wrap the content in Delayed to have it recomputed on each request instead of being deployed as a static result.

tools.name: CloudImport
tools.description: Imports data from a cloud object using the same format machinery as Import. It handles CSV, JSON, images and all other supported formats. Use it to read data files kept in the cloud.

tools.name: CloudExport
tools.description: Exports an expression to a cloud object in a specified format, returning the CloudObject. Permissions can be set at the same time. Use it to publish data files and images to a URL.

tools.name: EmbedCode
tools.description: Generates code in an external language such as JavaScript, Python or Java that calls a deployed API. It handles parameter marshalling and the HTTP request. Use it to hand integration code to developers working outside Wolfram.

tools.name: Permissions
tools.description: Option controlling who may read, execute or modify a cloud object, from "Private" through "Public" to explicit per-user rules. It is set at deployment time or changed later with SetOptions. Getting it right is essential before sharing a URL.
tools.notes: PermissionsKey allows access via a secret key without requiring a Wolfram account.

tools.name: PermissionsKey
tools.description: Represents a secret key that grants access to a cloud object without requiring the visitor to sign in. The key is appended to the URL as a query parameter. Use it for semi-private sharing of deployments.

tools.name: ScheduledTask
tools.description: Defines a computation to be run automatically on a schedule, either locally or in the cloud. Schedules can be intervals, specific times or cron-like specifications. Use it for periodic data collection, reports and monitoring.
tools.notes: TaskExecute runs a task immediately; TaskSuspend, TaskResume and TaskRemove control its lifecycle.

tools.name: TaskExecute
tools.description: Runs a scheduled or background task immediately, without waiting for its next scheduled time. It is the quickest way to test that a task works. The task remains scheduled afterwards.

tools.name: URLShorten
tools.description: Creates a short URL that redirects to a longer cloud or external URL. Custom short names can be requested. Use it to make deployed links easier to share and print.

tools.name: GenerateHTTPResponse
tools.description: Converts an expression into a full HTTP response object, giving explicit control over status code, headers and content type. It is what cloud deployments use internally. Use it when a deployment must return non-default headers or status codes.
tools.notes: HTTPResponse constructs a response directly; HTTPRequestData gives access to the incoming request inside a deployment.

tools.name: HTTPRequestData
tools.description: Gives information about the HTTP request currently being served inside a cloud deployment, such as query parameters, headers, method and body. It lets deployed code adapt to the caller. Use it for custom routing and authentication logic.
